subject: Clarify Redwood role & evidence for CA resident routing and transient cache
messages:
From: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa.cheng@healthsync.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: legal_ops@healthsync.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft DPA + ask on routing/residency for CA residents

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking a look at our DPA draft (attached). We have a few open items specific to CA/CPRA that we need firm answers and evidence on before the next procurement milestone:

- Role affirmation: we need explicit language confirming Redwood will act solely as a "Service Provider" under CCPA/CPRA for HealthSync customer data, with no independent sale/use.
- Transient cache behavior: does prefix/KV caching ever persist PII beyond in-memory or disk-backed kv-caches? If so, please describe persistence windows and controls.
- Routing & residency: HealthSync requires that requests originating from CA-resident accounts be routed to US-only capacity and not transit to EU/APAC for inference. Can you provide an architecture diagram and operational routing policy?
- Subprocessor residency attestation: list of subprocessors plus whether any subprocessors process CA data outside the US. We may need an attestation letter on residency for in-scope subprocessors.
- Telemetry vs billing: we need delineation of telemetry used for service improvement vs telemetry retained for billing and audit — retention windows for each.

Attaching our redline. Can you respond to each bullet and include any supporting artifacts (dataflow diagram, subprocessor list, SOC2 report link)? If helpful, we'd like to book a 30-minute call this week.

Attachments: HealthSync_DPA_draft_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Alyssa Cheng
Sr. Legal Ops | HealthSync

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa.cheng@healthsync.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 12:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + ask on routing/residency for CA residents

Alyssa — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary answers below; details + artifacts attached.

1) Role affirmation
- Short answer: Redwood will accept and sign language that we are a "Service Provider" (CPRA/CCPA) for HealthSync customer data. We will not sell data or use it for ad-targeting. Suggested clause: "Redwood Inference is a Service Provider as defined by the CCPA/CPRA and will process Personal Information solely on behalf of HealthSync pursuant to documented instructions."

2) Transient cache behavior
- Our runtime uses a combination of in-memory KV caches and ephemeral disk spill for high-request workloads. By default these caches are not retained as customer-identifiable logs beyond the request lifetime. We do persist minimal transient artifacts for performance for up to 6 hours in edge cases (configurable). We can provide a configuration option to set the persistence window to 0 (no disk spill) for in-scope data. See redwood-dataflow-mapping.pdf.

3) Routing & residency
- We support policy-based routing. For CA-resident tenant IDs we can pin traffic to US-only regions and will document the routing policy in the DPA exhibit. Attachment includes an architecture diagram and the policy statement we propose.

4) Subprocessor residency
- Attached is our current subprocessor list and country mappings. A small number of telemetry/storage providers operate in multiple regions; none of the core inference runtime subprocessors perform inference outside the US for pinned HealthSync CA traffic if you enable the US-only routing flag. We can provide a residency attestation letter for subprocessors that will be in-scope.

5) Telemetry vs billing
- We classify telemetry into: Operational telemetry (latency, error rates), Billing telemetry (token counts, invoiceable metrics), and Quality telemetry (prompt/eval traces). Billing telemetry is retained for 18 months by default for invoicing; operational telemetry 90 days; quality telemetry is kept only if customer opts into eval sharing (explicit). We can reduce billing retention to 12 months for HealthSync.

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-mapping.pdf, redwood-subprocessor-export.csv, SOC2-Redwood-link.txt

If you want, Kimberly and Karthik from our legal/infra teams are happy to join a 30-min call to walk through the technical exhibit.

— Rafael Mendes
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa.cheng@healthsync.com>, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + ask on routing/residency for CA residents

Alyssa — adding a few operational commitments we can include as DPA exhibits so the legal team has concrete obligations rather than loose promises:

- Residency exhibit: we will include an explicit table that maps HealthSync tenant IDs/regions to enforced routing policies and the list of datacenter regions used. This will be an appendix updated on a quarterly cadence.
- Cache control exhibit: we will add an operational control that when "US-only" residency is enabled for a tenant, persistent disk spill for KV caches is disabled and in-memory only caching is enforced; fallback to disk requires pre-authorized escalation.
- Subprocessor attestation: Redwood will provide (a) current subprocessor list with country processing locations, and (b) an attestation letter for those subprocessors stating expected residency for the next 12 months. If a subprocessor plans to relocate processing for HealthSync CA traffic outside the US, Redwood will notify HealthSync within 30 days and offer mitigation (onshore fallback or migration plan).
- Billing trace carveout: billing token counts will be retained for invoicing; where possible we will pseudonymize billing traces and provide aggregated billing exports. Retention for billing traces can be set to 12 months for HealthSync.

We will circulate DPA exhibit language today. Rafael / Karthik — can you confirm the engineering feasibility of the cache-control fallback window and the quarterly exhibit updates?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Associate Counsel | Redwood Inference
